introduction_markdown:
Answer both questions beginning each answer on a new page in the answer booklet. Both answers carry equal marks.

Credit will be given for accuracy, correct use of a variety of expressions, verbs, vocabulary and idioms.

Use blue ink only.

You are reminded of the necessity for orderly presentation of your answers.
enonce_intro_markdown:
*Using a tense suitable to your chosen topic, write an essay in French, of at least 140 and not more than 150 words, (not counting figures, words in brackets, abbreviations and names of people or places) on ONE of the following topics.*

*Credit will be given for the correct use of a variety of expressions, verbs, vocabulary and idioms.*

*If you choose topic (b), your name must be Atalaku and your address Lycée de Ntoh.*

*If you choose topic (c), your essay must be based on the events in the pictures.*

*Off-topic material will earn no marks.*

Le sujet (b) dit « Vous venez de vous absenter d'un cours de français ce matin parce que vous êtes venu en retard » : la logique est ambiguë (absent du cours à cause du retard) ; le corrigé retient que le professeur n'a pas laissé l'élève entrer. Le prénom de l'ami (Paul) est inventé.

questions.corrige_markdown:
**Tense chosen:** the passé composé for what happened this morning, with the imparfait for the circumstances (the lessons began at 7.30, the streets were crowded). The text is a letter to a friend, so it has a place and date, an informal salutation (*Cher Paul*), a body, a closing formula and the signature *Atalaku*; the address *Lycée de Ntoh* is the one required by the topic, and *tu* is used because the reader is a friend.

**Model essay** (146 words, counted with the heading and signature; 141 without the names of people and places and the figure)

Lycée de Ntoh, le lundi 5 octobre

Cher Paul,

Je t'écris pour t'expliquer pourquoi je n'ai pas assisté au cours de français ce matin, lundi. Hier soir, j'ai révisé très tard et ce matin mon réveil n'a pas sonné. Je me suis réveillé à sept heures, alors que les cours commençaient à sept heures trente.

Je me suis habillé en vitesse et j'ai couru jusqu'à la route. Les rues étaient pleines de monde et j'avais très peur d'arriver en retard. Il n'y avait aucun taxi, alors j'ai demandé à un motard de m'emmener. Il a roulé très vite et nous sommes arrivés au lycée à huit heures.

Le professeur ne m'a pas laissé entrer et j'ai attendu dehors, honteux. À la fin du cours, il m'a écouté, puis il m'a pardonné et il m'a donné la leçon à copier. Peux-tu me prêter ton cahier ?

Ton ami,

Atalaku

**Notes**

The letter follows the three bullet points: the circumstances and the day (paragraph 1: Monday, the alarm clock did not ring), what the writer did to reach school (paragraph 2: ran to the road, asked a motorcycle rider for a lift), how the teacher reacted and how it ended (paragraph 3: not allowed in, forgiven at the end of the lesson, a lesson to copy). The name Atalaku and the address Lycée de Ntoh are imposed by the topic; the friend's first name (Paul) is invented, and names of people and places are not counted in the word limit. The writer is a boy (*réveillé*, *habillé*, *honteux*).

**Marking criteria**

| Criterion | What earns the marks |
|---|---|
| Accuracy | Correct verb forms, agreements, spelling and accents; correct use of the tense chosen |
| Variety of expressions | Linking words (*d'abord*, *puis*, *finalement*, *heureusement*) and set phrases |
| Variety of verbs | Several different verbs instead of *être*, *avoir* and *faire* only |
| Vocabulary and idioms | Words and expressions suited to the topic; idioms used correctly |
| Relevance and length | All three bullet points covered; between 140 and 150 words |

**Common mistakes**

1. Forgetting the letter format (address, date, salutation, closing) or not using the imposed name and address.
2. Using the wrong register: the letter goes to a friend, so *tu* and an informal closing (*Ton ami*) are expected, not *vous* and *Veuillez agréer ...*.
